summary: Deepfake videos of Italy's prime minister and president promoted a fraudulent crypto investment with a promised guaranteed income and a 250-euro entry deposit. Italy's market regulator blocked the ads and four sites, its first use of new powers.
technical_summary: Generated video impersonating Italian officials was used in advertisements steering viewers to fake trading platforms, where victims are guided by phone to deposit money and shown fabricated gains. The regulator ordered the ads and sites blocked.

summary: Turkish police arrested nine suspects accused of using AI-generated videos to defraud about 33 people of roughly 15 million lira. Six were jailed pending trial and three were released under judicial supervision.
technical_summary: Suspects allegedly produced synthetic videos with unnamed AI tools to deceive victims into handing over money, in coordinated cases across several Turkish provinces.

summary: Indian journalist Ravish Kumar warned that several YouTube channels were using AI imitations of his face and voice to read fabricated, nonsensical news in his name. He filed complaints with YouTube and was awaiting action.
technical_summary: Voice and likeness cloning were used to create synthetic presenter videos that pass as a well-known journalist, published on multiple YouTube channels without his consent, creating false attribution of news content.

summary: In March 2020 Facebook wrongly blocked users from posting legitimate news articles about the coronavirus, which its spam filter flagged. Facebook said it was a bug unrelated to moderator staffing changes and began restoring the posts.
technical_summary: An automated anti-spam classifier misclassified links to reputable news outlets as spam and removed or blocked them. A former executive speculated it was linked to reduced human moderation; Facebook denied this and attributed it to a system bug.

technology.quote: this is a bug in an anti-spam system, unrelated to any changes in our content moderator workforce

failure_mode.quote: Facebook is blocking users from posting some legitimate news articles about the novel coronavirus

affected_population.quote: multiple Facebook users reported on Twitter that they found themselves unable to post articles

notes: Whether reduced human moderation contributed was speculation that Facebook denied.

summary: A Mumbai businessman lost Rs 80,000 after a caller posing as an embassy official claimed his son was arrested and played a cloned voice resembling the son pleading for help. He transferred money before checking with his son.
technical_summary: Fraudsters used AI voice cloning to simulate a family member in distress during an urgent impersonation call, exploiting fear to prevent verification and prompting a rapid payment via a mobile payment app.

technology.quote: AI voice cloning technology allows fraudsters to create realistic replicas of a person's voice

failure_mode.quote: Voice cloning tools are readily available online, putting this deceptive power in the hands of anyone with malicious intent

harm_type.quote: lost Rs 80,000 after being tricked by a fraudster impersonating his son and a representative from the Indian Embassy in Dubai

affected_population.quote: A 68-year-old businessman from Powai fell victim to an artificial intelligence voice cloning scam, losing Rs80,000

summary: At an international AIDS conference, a U.S. State Department presentation displayed a map of Africa with every country mislabeled. Analysis found an AI watermark linked to OpenAI tools, and the department took responsibility, saying a team member hastily edited the slide.
technical_summary: A map slide apparently produced with a generative image tool contained wrong geographic labels, showing the tool cannot reliably render factual maps. The error passed through review and was displayed to an international audience.

failure_mode.quote: A U.S. government map of Africa mislabeled every country during a State Department presentation
the map had been produced by a team member who hastily changed the slide deck before the event

harm_type.quote: full responsibility for the confusion and misrepresentation it caused for attendees

notes: AI involvement rests on a watermark found by Reuters; OpenAI said it was investigating.

summary: Open-source projects including KDE, GNOME, SourceHut and Fedora reported outages and added costs from aggressive AI crawlers that ignored crawling rules and disguised their traffic. Some projects adopted proof-of-work challenges or blocked whole countries.
technical_summary: Automated crawlers collecting data for AI model training ignore robots.txt, spoof user agents and rotate IP addresses, hitting expensive endpoints such as git history pages. The load overwhelms volunteer-run infrastructure and cannot be easily distinguished from human traffic.

harm_type.quote: KDE GitLab infrastructure was overwhelmed by another AI crawler, with IPs from an Alibaba range

notes: Attribution to specific AI companies is not established for most reported incidents.

summary: Microsoft's news aggregation service displayed an AI-generated poll beside a Guardian story about a woman's death, asking readers to choose between murder, accident or suicide. Readers blamed the Guardian, which said its reputation was harmed; Microsoft disabled such polls.
technical_summary: An automated feature generated a speculative poll attached to a sensitive news article without editorial review. The system had no safeguard to block insensitive content on tragedies, and the poll remained for several days.

harm_type.quote: caused “significant reputational damage” to the organisation

notes: Deceased woman not named. The model behind the poll was not specified.

summary: Researchers identified about 20 inauthentic YouTube channels using AI-generated scripts, voiceovers and visuals to pose as Albertans and push false claims about Alberta separatism and U.S. annexation, drawing nearly 40 million views.
technical_summary: A coordinated network of channels mass-produced generative-AI videos with synthetic voiceovers, old news clips and fabricated polls, presenting political claims as settled. The operators and their motives were not determined and may include ad revenue.

summary: Researchers and reporters found Facebook feeds filling with AI-generated spam images, many used in scams or engagement bait, and that Facebook's recommendations were boosting some of these pages to users who did not follow them.
technical_summary: Pages posting AI-generated images at high volume exploit engagement-optimized recommendation, which surfaces the content to non-followers, where it draws reactions from users who believe it is real. Researchers link many pages to scams and spam.

summary: Scammers circulated a deepfake ad showing a broadcaster being assaulted to promote a fake 'Quantum AI' investment scheme using her husband's name, finance expert Martin Lewis. He said the couple received worried messages and that she was unharmed.
